rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The essay at a glance "Knowledge and Wisdom" by Bertrand Russell is a philosopher's attempt to separate two words the modern world uses interchangeably — and the separation is the essay's whole argument. Knowledge, Russell says, is what can be taught and examined: facts, skills, methods.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Knowledge without wisdom is dangerous — define both terms separately.
Wisdom components: breadth of feeling, awareness of ends, emancipation from bias.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: Definition of wisdom: the capacity to consider the TOTAL effect of actions and emancipation from personal prejudice — memorise the two components.  ·  ## The themes worth an essay **Knowledge without wisdom is dangerous** — the central theme: capacity enlarges consequence, so judgment, not information, is the scarce resource. **The specialist's blindness** — the conceptual heart: mastery of a fragment without a sense of the whole produces the modern world's most confident errors.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. How does Russell define knowledge? (2 marks)** A. As the accumulation of information and skill: facts, techniques and methods that can be taught, learned and examined. Knowledge, in his definition, is capacity — and capacity alone says nothing about the ends it serves. **Q. How does Russell define wisdom? (2 marks)** A.…  ·  ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. "Knowledge without wisdom is power without aim." Discuss with reference to Russell's examples. (8 marks)** A model answer builds from the definitions (knowledge as capacity, wisdom as judgment) and works the examples as proofs: the technician whose skill serves health or plague depending on the ends chosen; the specialist whose fragment-mastery blinds him to the whole; the historical…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Distinguish knowledge and wisdom as Russell does. (2 marks) — knowledge is information/skill; wisdom is using it for the widest good.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The argument, step by step The essay opens by defining its two terms with a philosopher's economy: knowledge is the accumulation of information and skill; wisdom is the right application of knowledge to living — the choice of ends as well as means.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Definition and distinction** — the essay's master method: two terms sharpened against each other until the boundary is visible, and the boundary is the argument. - **Exemplification** — the essay's power supply: the technician, the specialist, the historical case — each example a proof that knowledge's value depends on the wisdom directing it.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Russell's thesis: knowledge without wisdom is dangerous — technical skill must serve humane ends; state it in one sentence.  ·  Trick 2: His examples are the essay: scientists building weapons, pharmacists, transport experts — quote two examples showing knowledge misused.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. Give one of Russell's examples of knowledge without wisdom. (1 mark) — specialists improving weapons of destruction.
